title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operating in Austin struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood while in autonomous mode, with a human safety operator in the vehicle. The car did not slow down or stop before impact. This represents a failure in the perception or decision-making systems to recognize and avoid a small living obstacle in an urban setting where pedestrians and animals are present.

The incident occurred during normal deployment in a neighborhood where the system was being tested. A human operator was present but did not intervene. It is not established whether the operator could have prevented the collision or whether the vehicle's sensors detected the duck before impact.

The company's response included adjusting its testing area and stating it would evaluate technology improvements and simulation testing. Whether these measures address the underlying detection or avoidance failure is not established.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. Residents had become attached to this particular duck because it was nesting near a local Italian restaurant. A neighborhood resident posted about the incident on Facebook, and the story gained local media attention, raising concerns about whether autonomous vehicles should operate in residential areas.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and denied a resident's claim that it failed to stop at a stop sign. The company has since adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake. Additionally, local residents collected the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator for safekeeping. Avride stated it is evaluating technology improvements to prevent similar situations, including conducting simulation experiments to ensure any changes maintain vehicle safety performance in other driving scenarios.
